scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Hitch hike was a prominent dance craze of the 1960s.

It was initiated by the 1962 Marvin Gaye hit 'Hitch Hike' and experienced a second wave of popularity in 1969 following the release of Vanity Fare's 'Hitchin' a Ride.' Since its inception, the move has transitioned from a standalone fad into a standard element of various line, club, and jazz dance styles.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: As a fad dance, it was primarily used for social entertainment and group participation.
It represents the 1960s trend of creating dances based on literal, everyday gestures.
It has since become a nostalgic marker of that era's pop culture.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is based on the hitchhiking gesture of waving a stuck-out thumb.
The standard Motown sequence consists of waving the right thumb over the right shoulder three times, followed by a clap, then repeating the same sequence with the left thumb and another clap.
This is performed alongside shimmying body ripples.
Watch for The Thumb Wave, The Motown Clap.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Marvin Gaye is the central figure responsible for the dance's origin through his 1962 song.
The group Vanity Fare is credited with refueling the dance's popularity in 1969.
While the core move is consistent, it has been adapted into disco, jazz, and various club dances.
The Hitch hike is a descendant of the 1960s fad dance movement.
